missionPremise: The gate G-95 built is good and was not yet a CONTROL, because its headline number depended on two conditions nobody had declared, and both were found by rendering lanes measuring rather than by the gate reporting. Sources: R3-F2 (`_inbox/2026-08-19_r3_close.json`) measured the Development services lens at 0 color-contrast nodes at 1440x900 and 2 at 1440x3000 on one commit; R2-F6 and R2-F7 (`_inbox/2026-08-19_r2_close.json`) measured the same viewport bound independently and measured the gate FAILING locally on Windows with 44 unresolved nodes while the same SHA's CI check-run concluded success; G-95's own REVIEW_ITEMS entry (`_inbox/2026-08-19_g95_close.json`) records the environment dependence and measured it in the OPPOSITE direction, 2 on Linux and 0 on Windows. A figure that ranges 0 to 88 across two operating systems, and that covers only what was above the fold, is a control-design question and not a tuning one - and it is going into an Accessibility Conformance Report, which is a legal document an auditor will not read at our viewport. SECOND PREMISE, delivered mid-lane by the coordinator from sibling lane K1 and accepted: a contrast defect at roughly a third of the required ratio was invisible to the gate entirely, and an adjudication resting on reasoning rather than measurement is the same defect class sitting inside the instrument.
completionPredicate: A stranger runs the gate, reads its number, and cannot avoid reading the two conditions that make the number true: which viewports it covers and what fraction of the product's rendered text each one reached, and which environment is the figure of record with the witness that lets a disagreeing machine be diagnosed from one log line. An unresolved check reads as unresolved and never as a pass. Every class the gate refuses on carries a plant and a bare-Node firing proof. The G-95 properties all still hold, each one exercised. The CI check-run conclusion string on the head SHA is the authority, and the branch is open for a planner merge rather than merged. All of that is met and evidenced below with raw output; the two things NOT met are named in whatRemainsOpen rather than narrated away.

The final diff is FOUR files and src/a11y-surfaces.mjs is untouched - the surface list needed no change, because it was already derived and the viewport axis belongs to the scanner rather than to the surface list. No file under web/ is modified, which matters more than usual here: the two defects this lane made visible both live in web/, and the correct output was a measurement and a routing rather than an edit. Deliberately out of scope and untouched: web/index.html, web/shell.css, web/app.js, web/sc-kit.css, live Bastrop, G-52, G-24, L26, and every other lane's clone. Also deliberately NOT done: the aria-hidden fix on the separator, which is a web/ edit and is routed with its evidence instead.

mechanism2_theEnvironment_NAMEDWITHEVIDE.theMechanism: The identical probe string measures 225.00px on Linux and 228.33px on Windows - 1.48% wider for the same loaded face, which is glyph rasterisation and subpixel advance rounding. The consequence is exact and it is legible in the witness: the FOOTER is identical between the two runs (navFootTop 601, navFootHeight 299, provHeight 274, demonstratedTop 640 on both), and what moves is the NAV LIST - lastNavItemBottom 698 against 718, a 20px difference, carrying overlapPx from 97 to 117 and navHiddenPx from 98 to 118. A nav item's bottom edge sits 20px further down on Windows, across the footer figures' boxes. axe samples the element stack at the centre of EACH text line box (getRectStack2, axe.js:24678) and sets elmPartiallyObscuring when those stacks disagree (filteredRectStack, axe.js:24710-24713). Partial overlap fires; full coverage and no coverage both resolve. 2 unresolved nodes on Linux, 134 on Windows, one commit.

whatWasBUILTInResponse: A SECOND INSTRUMENT. The scanner composites backgrounds and computes WCAG ratios itself for declared element groups, independent of axe and therefore of axe's exclusion set. Conservative by construction - it computes only where the answer is unambiguous and counts everything else as could-not-compute, reported and never scored either way. It applies the large-text threshold. It excludes [aria-hidden=true] text and COUNTS what it excludes, because an exclusion nobody can see the size of is indistinguishable from a blind spot, which is the entire lesson.

MEASURED ADJUDICATIONS. An entry claiming a pair reads acceptably carries measuredRatio and a threshold; the scanner recomputes exactly those subjects every run; the verdict REFUSES the entry when the run's own measurement falls below the threshold, and prints a note when it drifts while still clearing.

TWO PLANTS. punctuation-contrast plants the class axe cannot see; adjudication-refuted repaints the adjudicated subjects below threshold and leaves the ledger alone, so the gate must refuse its own entry.

theARIAHIDDENRECOMMENDATION.verdict: AGREE, with one measured caveat and one condition. aria-hidden="true" on the .sep span alone is right: the glyph is a visual separator carrying no information a screen reader needs, the surrounding text stays parseable without it, and text that is pure decoration is outside 1.4.3's scope.
theARIAHIDDENRECOMMENDATION.theCaveat: MEASURED: aria-hidden does NOT satisfy axe. In the same bisect, an element with real text at a failing pair returns VIOLATION with aria-hidden=true set exactly as without it. So it is a correctness and accessibility-tree fix, not a tool-silencing one - and the only reason it will read as resolved here is that THIS gate's exclusion set is declared and counts what it excludes.
theARIAHIDDENRECOMMENDATION.theCondition: if the separator is to stay in the accessibility tree, the decoration exception does not apply and the colour must go to 4.5:1 instead. One or the other, never neither.
